clue.text: At university he brought back rock, causing turmoil

parts.note: being up means being in residence at university
taken as written

indicators.note: brought back signals that the word for rock is read from right to left

parts.note: lava is molten rock that has cooled and set

explanation.surface: A student's rock music sparks chaos on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' wants to be music, but it is molten stone; 'brought back' turns it to AVAL at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent upheaval is a great disturbance, which is the same idea as turmoil.

clue.text: Peacekeepers lacking support, except if…

annotationWithheld.why: Peacekeepers lacking support, except if… (6): UN + LESS (lacking) gives the answer, but 'support' has no job in the parse

clue.text: … the Commons keep the members together

parts.note: the House of Commons is called the House
to hold is to keep

explanation.surface: Parliament keeps its MPs united.
explanation.walkthrough: Continues from 1 down: the Commons is the House in the UK Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A household is all the people living together in one home, a family unit.

clue.text: Apply for opening, keeping husband in the same place

indicators.note: keeping says the opening holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: an adit is a horizontal entrance or opening to a mine
ib. is the short form of ibidem, Latin for in the same place, used in footnotes

explanation.surface: Someone requests an entrance while keeping a spouse where they are.
explanation.walkthrough: ADIT holds H and IB; 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhibit is a formal word meaning to apply or affix.

clue.text: Grown-up daughter featured in article last month

indicators.note: featured in places the daughter's letter inside the others

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
ult., short for ultimo, means last month in old letter-writing

explanation.surface: An adult daughter appeared in a magazine piece last month.
explanation.walkthrough: D goes inside A and ULT.
explanation.definitionFit: An adult is a person who is fully grown.

clue.text: Go about with West End composer

indicators.note: the end of the word West is its final letter

parts.note: Maurice Ravel was the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: Someone tours London's theatre district in the company of a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' reads as London's theatre district, but it means the last letter of West, T.
explanation.definitionFit: To travel is to journey from place to place, to go about.

clue.text: Impress greenhorn

explanation.definitionFit: To recruit is to enlist, as a press-gang would impress men, and a recruit is a novice newcomer.

clue.text: It's bound to be an undercroft

explanation.definitionFit: A vault is a leap or bound, and also an arched cellar or crypt beneath a building.

clue.text: Ability to read illuminated English of a lively type

parts.note: lit means lighted up, illuminated
racy means lively and spirited

explanation.surface: A vivid English illuminated manuscript in a lively script.
explanation.definitionFit: Literacy is the skill of reading and writing.

clue.text: Abandoned in favour of Japanese drink with new top

annotationWithheld.why: Abandoned in favour of Japanese drink with new top (8): FOR + SAKE + N gives the answer, but 'top' has no job in the parse, and N sits at the foot not the top
annotationWithheld.clue: Abandoned in favour of Japanese drink with new top

clue.text: Ridicule a tough lout for initiating unsuccessful crime

annotationWithheld.why: Ridicule a tough lout for initiating unsuccessful crime (5,3,2,5): fodder A TOUGH LOUT FOR plus U and C (first letters of unsuccessful crime) gives the letters, but no separate word signals the anagram, so one word would do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Ridicule a tough lout for initiating unsuccessful crime

clue.text: In 'Hard Times' her better half provided a drink

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: In a Dickens novel, a wife supplies something to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her better half' suggests a spouse; the answer runs across TimeS HER BETter. Hard Times is a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherbet was once a cooling fruit drink of the Middle East, and in Britain a fizzy powder drink.

clue.text: Stroll with relative in southern outskirts of Esher

indicators.note: in places the relative inside the letters formed around it
the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A walk with a family member around the edge of a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: Esher is a well-off town in Surrey, south-west of London; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To saunter is to walk in a slow, leisurely way, a stroll.

clue.text: Frank position taken by member with boat

parts.note: a post is a job or position
M is the abbreviation for member, as in Member of Parliament
Noah's ark was a boat

explanation.surface: A man named Frank takes up a post aboard a boat as a crew member.
explanation.definitionFit: To frank a letter is to mark it as paid, which is what a postal stamp mark does.

clue.text: Politician in unusually halting type of Commons session

indicators.note: in places the politician's letter inside the rearranged word
unusually says the letters of halting come in an odd order

parts.note: L stands for Liberal, a politician of that party

explanation.surface: A politician speaking with unusual hesitation in a parliamentary sitting.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes into ALNIGHT, made by 'unusually' from HALTING.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-night sitting is a parliamentary session continuing through the night.

clue.text: Subject excludes king from circle

indicators.note: excludes says the letter for king is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a tropic is a circle of latitude round the globe
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A topic of talk keeps the monarch out of the social circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is a subject of discussion or writing.

clue.text: Once he's got the key, he can put his coat on

definitions.text: Once he's got the key, he can put his coat on

parts.words: Once he's got the key, he can put his coat on
parts.note: a key is the roughened surface that lets a layer of render grip a wall, and the coat is that layer, not clothing

explanation.surface: A man unlocks the door and then dons his jacket to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who applies smooth coats of render to walls and ceilings.

clue.text: One who sang Schubert's song in Titipu?

definitions.text: One who sang Schubert's song in Titipu?

parts.words: One who sang Schubert's song in Titipu?
parts.note: in The Mikado, set in the Japanese town of Titipu, Nanki-Poo disguises himself as a wandering singer; Schubert also wrote a song of that title

explanation.surface: Asks who performed a Schubert song in a Gilbert and Sullivan town.
explanation.walkthrough: Titipu is the town of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera The Mikado, where the hero sings 'A wandering minstrel I'.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval singer or musician who performed songs and verse.

clue.text: State's current retraction of benefit

parts.note: in means fashionable or current

indicators.note: retraction, a drawing back, means the word for benefit is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help or benefit

explanation.surface: A government's present withdrawal of welfare payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retraction of' turns the help word to DIA; the 's after State is a link meaning 'is', and 'current' is fashionable, not electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a country, a nation state.

clue.text: Contract made in a game

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A deal is struck during a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge players bid for contracts, so the surface sense of contract as a bid also hides the definition, to shorten.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge is to shorten or condense, as to contract a text.

clue.text: Crave 25 dn's container vessel

parts.note: to long for is to crave
25 down is SAUCE, and a gravy or sauce boat holds it

explanation.surface: Wanting a container for the sauce.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to the dish answering 25 down; its holder is a sauce boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A longboat is the large rowing boat carried on a sailing ship, a vessel.

clue.text: Adaption of the Bard which makes us beam

indicators.note: an adaption of a work reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare adaptation that makes the audience smile broadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beam' looks like smiling; it is a ship's width.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's beam is its width at the widest point.

clue.text: Worker taking poor lad in to parish officer

indicators.note: taking says the worker holds the rearranged letters inside it

parts.note: a worker bee is the classic crossword worker

indicators.note: poor says the letters of lad are in bad shape and rearranged

explanation.surface: A labourer brings a needy boy to the local official.
explanation.walkthrough: BEE holds ADL, which 'poor' makes from LAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle was a minor official of a church parish who kept order.

clue.text: Man taking old city — first-class officer

parts.note: Sam is a man's name
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
A1 means first-class, and the 1 reads as the letter I

explanation.surface: A soldier captures an ancient city and is a top-rank commander.
explanation.definitionFit: A samurai was a Japanese military retainer, a member of the warrior class.

clue.text: Light brown vessel crossing river out east

indicators.note: crossing says the vessel goes across, outside, the river's letters

parts.note: MY stands for motor yacht, a vessel

indicators.note: out says the letter for east is removed from the river's name

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: A tan-coloured boat crosses a river heading out eastwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is a river in Yorkshire; 'out' drops its E to leave OUS, and a motor yacht is written MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousy describes a dull, greyish-brown hair colour.

clue.text: Unusual respect for the staff

indicators.note: unusual says the letters of the next word appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Employees are treated with uncommon esteem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is a ceremonial staff or rod held by a monarch.

clue.text: Dish mostly used for relish

indicators.note: mostly says most of the word is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: a saucer is a small dish

explanation.surface: A plate mainly put to use for condiments.
explanation.definitionFit: A relish is a condiment or savoury accompaniment, like a sauce.

clue.text: We'd bend over backwards to avoid seeming so posturally challenged!

definitions.text: We'd bend over backwards to avoid seeming so posturally challenged!

parts.words: We'd bend over backwards to avoid seeming so posturally challenged!
parts.note: going to great lengths is taken literally: arching the spine backwards counters a forward stoop of the upper back

explanation.surface: We would try very hard not to look as though we have bad posture.
explanation.definitionFit: Having stooped upper body and a forward-curving back is a posture problem.

clue.text: They lack orders, having no specialised knowledge

explanation.definitionFit: Lay people are not ordained into holy orders, and laymen are non-experts in a profession.

clue.text: This swimmer is upright in the main

definitions.text: This swimmer is upright in the main

parts.words: This swimmer is upright in the main
parts.note: a fish that swims vertically in the ocean, the main being an old word for the sea, with a head shaped like a stallion

explanation.surface: Mostly, this swimmer is a decent sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upright in the main' reads as 'honest, mostly'; really it is a fish that swims vertically in the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fish with a horse-like head that swims standing upright.
